analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. No concrete regression is established in this scope. DaemonStateFile.swift:105-107,354-356 adds an optional add-on snapshot without changing persistence or existing trust fields. LifecycleMailbox.swift:28-54 extends the existing mailbox and preserves atomic claiming, PID/start-time filenames, owner-only directory checks, no-follow opens and bounded reads (57-87). AddonCommand.swift:70-99 verifies a fresh live process identity and add-on support, correlates replies by request ID and bounds waiting to ten seconds; Darkbloom.swift:32 registers this CLI surface. Lease validation and explicit force-release warnings are present. These controls do not authenticate same-owner software against ADV-001, but the evidence does not establish a new privilege or plaintext exposure.
ProviderDrain.swift:18,20-33 keeps admission closed during holds, lets lifecycle stop preempt them, and permits App Attest recovery to treat holds differently from service changes. Integration must verify callers do not use refusingForServiceChange as inference admission authorization, and that releasing a hold during reconnect/update cannot reopen service prematurely (TB-002, TB-011, T-052/T-053/T-057). The add-on request types, daemon handlers and socket/lock implementation are outside this batch: verify target/freshness and lease validation, socket peer authorization, bounded hold lifetime, cancellation/unload ordering and force-release behavior under VM memory contention (TB-003, TB-007, T-010/T-028/T-029). Also inspect the new snapshot's fields for prompt/key or stable-identity disclosure (A-001/A-003, T-058). No supplied change modifies encryption, billing, cache scoping or SSD crypto (T-008/T-041); hold-related cache cleanup and memory release remain integration questions, not demonstrated missing controls.
